requirements.requirement: RabbitMQ cluster spans node1, node2, and node3
requirements.summary: After a failed automatic peer-discovery attempt (blocked by firewall), node2 and node3 were reset and explicitly joined to node1 via rabbitmqctl join_cluster; cluster_status on node1 shows all three as Disk Nodes and Running Nodes. This was reconfirmed after the full restart cycle.

requirements.requirement: AMQP is served over TLS using a certificate authority created for this cluster
requirements.summary: A fresh self-signed CA ('RabbitMQ Cluster CA') was generated on node1 and used to issue per-node server certs with correct SANs. rabbitmq.conf sets listeners.tcp=none and listeners.ssl.default=5671 with the CA-issued server cert/key; ss/rabbitmqctl status confirms only a TLS listener on 5671 with no plaintext 5672 listener present on any node.

requirements.requirement: Only clients presenting a certificate issued by the cluster CA can connect
requirements.summary: ssl_options.verify=verify_peer and fail_if_no_peer_cert=true were configured. A handshake attempt with no client certificate was rejected with a 'certificate required' TLS alert, a rogue self-signed certificate was rejected with a 'Bad Certificate' alert (both confirmed in the RabbitMQ log), and a CA-issued client certificate completed the handshake and supported a full AMQP publish/consume via pika+mTLS on all three nodes.

requirements.requirement: Management interface (15672) reachable only from within the cluster
requirements.summary: Management was bound to each node's own 10.100.48.x cluster address (not 0.0.0.0) and firewalld rich rules restrict TCP/15672 (and 4369/25672) to the 10.100.48.0/24 subnet, with the general zone otherwise limited to ssh/cockpit/dhcpv6-client. A cross-node request from node2 to node1:15672 succeeded (200 OK), demonstrating intra-cluster reachability. However, no test was captured from a source outside the 10.100.48.0/24 subnet (or a non-cluster network context) to directly confirm the interface is actually blocked externally; the only evidence of exclusion is the firewall policy listing itself, not an observed rejected connection, so full enforcement is inferred rather than directly demonstrated.

overall_summary: The executor built a genuine 3-node RabbitMQ cluster on AlmaLinux 9 with AMQP served exclusively over TLS (listeners.tcp=none, TLS on 5671) using a cluster-dedicated CA, and directly demonstrated mutual-TLS enforcement: a no-cert handshake and a rogue self-signed cert were both rejected, while a CA-issued client cert completed the handshake and supported real publish/consume traffic on every node. Clustering was verified via rabbitmqctl cluster_status showing all three nodes as Disk/Running, both before and after a full one-at-a-time reboot cycle whose boot-id transitions match the fixed lifecycle snapshots exactly. The management-interface restriction is backed by solid configuration (per-node private IP binding, firewalld rich rules scoped to the cluster subnet) and one successful intra-cluster access test, but there is no captured evidence of a rejected request from outside the cluster subnet, so exclusion of external access is inferred from policy rather than directly observed. Hygiene is reasonable overall, with the tester/admin account and copies of sensitive TLS/client material (private key, password file) left behind in /tmp being the main unresolved residue.
limitations: No direct negative test was captured showing the management API is actually blocked from a source outside the 10.100.48.0/24 cluster subnet; exclusion relies on firewall/config inspection rather than an observed denied connection.

The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol (not part of the public task contract) was executed for all three nodes with clear pre/post boot-id changes matching the fixed lifecycle snapshots and recovered cluster/service/mTLS state, so it does not itself lower confidence in task functionality, but it is noted here for completeness.

Sensitive material (client private key, admin-equivalent password) was left in /tmp on the managed nodes after verification, which is a residual exposure risk though execution-bounded and low-blast-radius.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map directly to the task (package install, CA/cert generation, config, clustering, firewall, restart protocol). One join_cluster attempt (cmd-4969bc7908ba47a0) failed due to firewall blocking inter-node traffic and was cleanly corrected by a subsequent stop_app/reset/join_cluster/start_app sequence (cmd-e5a2061b3d5c445a) — this is an acceptable corrective retry, not residue. The main hygiene concern is that sensitive material was copied into /tmp for distribution to node2/node3 (CA cert, client1 cert+private key, an admin-equivalent test-user password file, and a test script) via cmd-63e1625966834925 and never cleaned up; the after-executor snapshot confirms /tmp/client1.key, /tmp/.tester_pw, /tmp/ca.crt, /tmp/client1.crt, and /tmp/amqp_test.py still present on node1 after the final restart, and a rogue self-signed test cert/key pair (/tmp/rogue.crt, /tmp/rogue.key) also remains. Leaving a client private key and a live user's password in a world-writable/readable temp directory is unnecessary residual exposure that should have been deleted after verification. The 'tester' administrator account created for verification (cmd-03b43414b66b47a1) was also left in place, which is a reasonable, low-risk artifact for a verification credential but adds to the residue tally.
